contexts.text: Interior and exterior scientifics are signified by the ears of the river Euphrates, even to the river of Egypt ().

The comparison with the blade, the ear, and the corn (), involves the rebirth of man by means of scientifics, the truths of faith, and the goods of charity... The blade = the first Scientific; the ear = the Scientific of truth thence derived; the corn = the good thence derived.
A ripening ear () = that they stood forth. Explained.
An ear, or ear containing the wheat or barley, = truths thus adjoined to goods.
A parched ear () = the good of charity; a green ear = the good of truth.
Standing corn = truth in conception; the ear, truth containing; and the wheat and barley in the ear, good receiving, and also received.
To gather the ears and eat them () = to be instructed in doctrinal things.

Corporeal things reformed... were represented by... a contexture... with points arranged into various beautiful forms... This little point was set in the forms. Afterwards, a more coherent form of such points, in beautiful forms, from minute points...

From the ear of the river even to the river of Egypt = all rational and scientific truth that would be of service to the Spiritual. An ear is mentioned, because it is the containant of corn, by which is signified the truth and good which is of service to the spiritual man for nourishment.
